content.content:
# Doxygen

Doxygen is the de facto standard tool for generating documentation from
annotated C++ sources, but it also supports other popular programming
languages such as C, Objective-C, C#, PHP, Java, Python, IDL
(Corba, Microsoft, and UNO/OpenOffice flavors), Fortran,
and to some extent D. Doxygen also supports the hardware description language VHDL.

## What Doxygen Does

Doxygen can help you in three ways:

1. It can generate an online documentation browser (in HTML) and/or an
   offline reference manual (in LaTeX) from a set of documented source files.
   There is also support for generating output in RTF (MS-Word), PostScript,
   hyperlinked PDF, compressed HTML, DocBook and Unix man pages.
   The documentation is extracted directly from the sources, which makes
   it much easier to keep the documentation consistent with the source code.

2. You can configure doxygen to extract the code structure from undocumented
   source files. This is very useful to quickly find your way in large
   source distributions. Doxygen can also visualize the relations between
   the various elements by means of include dependency graphs, inheritance
   diagrams, and collaboration diagrams, which are all generated automatically.

3. You can also use doxygen for creating normal documentation (as I did for
   the doxygen user manual and doxygen website).

## Usage

Doxygen is a command line based utility. Here are the main ways to use it:

### 1) Generate a template configuration file

```bash
doxygen [-s] -g [configName]
```

### 2) Update an existing configuration file

```bash
doxygen [-s] -u [configName]
```

### 3) Generate documentation using an existing configuration file

```bash
doxygen [configName]
```

### 4) Generate a template file that controls the layout of the generated documentation

```bash
doxygen -l [layoutFileName]
```

If layoutFileName is omitted, DoxygenLayout.xml will be used as the filename.
If - is used for layoutFileName, Doxygen writes to standard output.

### 5) Generate a template style sheet file for RTF, HTML or LaTeX

For RTF:
```bash
doxygen -w rtf styleSheetFile
```

For HTML:
```bash
doxygen -w html headerFile footerFile styleSheetFile [configFile]
```

For LaTeX:
```bash
doxygen -w latex headerFile footerFile styleSheetFile [configFile]
```

### 6) Generate an RTF extensions file

```bash
doxygen -e rtf extensionsFile
```

If - is used for extensionsFile Doxygen will write to standard output.

### 7) Compare the used configuration file with the template configuration file

```bash
doxygen -x [configFile]
```

Compare without replacing environment variables or CMake type replacement variables:
```bash
doxygen -x_noenv [configFile]
```

### 8) Show a list of built-in emojis

```bash
doxygen -f emoji outputFileName
```

If - is used for outputFileName Doxygen will write to standard output.

### Additional Options

- If `-s` is specified, the comments of the configuration items in the config file will be omitted.
- If configName is omitted, 'Doxyfile' will be used by default.
- If - is used for configFile, Doxygen will write/read the configuration to/from standard output/input.
- If `-q` is used for a Doxygen documentation run, Doxygen will see this as if QUIET=YES has been set.
- `-v` prints version string
- `-V` prints extended version information
- `-h`, `-?` prints usage help information
- `doxygen -d` prints additional usage flags for debugging purposes

## Download

The latest binaries and source code can be downloaded from:
* https://www.doxygen.nl/

## Documentation

Full documentation and manual:
* https://www.doxygen.nl/manual/

## Issues and Bug Reports

Use the issue tracker to report bugs:
* https://github.com/doxygen/doxygen/issues

## Mailing Lists

There are three mailing lists:

* doxygen-announce@lists.sourceforge.net - Announcement of new releases only
* doxygen-users@lists.sourceforge.net - for doxygen users
* doxygen-develop@lists.sourceforge.net - for doxygen developers

To subscribe follow the link to:
* https://sourceforge.net/projects/doxygen/

## Source Code

Doxygen is hosted at GitHub:
* https://github.com/doxygen/doxygen

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Parse observed `doxygen -g -` output into a structured tag table (JSON).

The input is *observed program output* captured from the reference binary's
normal CLI.  We turn it into a declarative table so our own generator can
reproduce -g / -s -g / -u / -x from one source of truth.
"""
import json, re, sys

def parse(full_path, short_path):
    lines = open(full_path, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
    if lines and lines[-1] == '': lines.pop()

    items = []          # ordered list of {kind: 'section'|'tag', ...}
    i = 0
    # header block: everything up to the first section separator
    header = []
    while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].startswith('#---'):
        header.append(lines[i]); i += 1

    pending = []        # comment lines awaiting a tag
    while i < len(lines):
        ln = lines[i]
        if ln.startswith('#---'):
            title = lines[i+1][1:].strip()
            items.append({'kind': 'section', 'title': title})
            i += 3
            continue
        if ln.startswith('#'):
            pending.append(ln[1:].rstrip() if ln != '#' else '')
            # strip exactly one leading space of the '# ' prefix
            if pending[-1].startswith(' '): pending[-1] = pending[-1][1:]
            i += 1
            continue
        if ln == '':
            i += 1
            continue
        m = re.match(r'^([A-Z_0-9]+)(\s*)=(.*)$', ln)
        assert m, f'unparsed line {i}: {ln!r}'
        name = m.group(1)
        vals = [m.group(3)]
        while vals[-1].endswith('\\'):
            i += 1
            vals.append(lines[i])
        items.append({'kind': 'tag', 'name': name, 'doc': pending,
                      'raw': [v for v in vals]})
        pending = []
        i += 1
    return header, items

def value_of(raw):
    """Reconstruct the logical value list from the raw wrapped lines."""
    parts = []
    for k, v in enumerate(raw):
        s = v
        if s.endswith('\\'): s = s[:-1]
        s = s.strip()
        if s: parts.append(s)
    return parts

def unquote(tok):
    if len(tok) >= 2 and tok[0] == '"' and tok[-1] == '"':
        return tok[1:-1]
    return tok

def tokenize(s):
    """Split a value string into quoted/unquoted tokens like doxygen does."""
    out, cur, inq = [], '', False
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        c = s[i]
        if c == '"':
            inq = not inq
            cur += c
        elif c in ' \t,' and not inq:
            if cur: out.append(cur); cur = ''
        else:
            cur += c
        i += 1
    if cur: out.append(cur)
    return out

def infer(item):
    doc = '\n'.join(item['doc'])
    vals = value_of(item['raw'])
    joined = ' '.join(vals)
    toks = [unquote(t) for t in tokenize(joined)]
    info = {'name': item['name'], 'doc': item['doc'], 'default': toks}
    mn = re.search(r'Minimum value: (-?\d+), maximum value: (-?\d+), default value: (-?\d+)\.', doc)
    pv = re.search(r'Possible values are: (.*?)(?:\.\n|\.$)', doc, re.S)
    dv = re.search(r'The default value is: (.*?)(?:\.\n|\.$)', doc, re.S)
    if mn:
        info['type'] = 'int'
        info['min'], info['max'] = int(mn.group(1)), int(mn.group(2))
    elif pv:
        raw_pv = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', pv.group(1))
        vs = [x.strip() for x in re.split(r',| and ', raw_pv) if x.strip()]
        info['type'] = 'enum'
        info['values'] = vs
    elif dv and re.sub(r'\s+',' ',dv.group(1)).strip() in ('YES','NO'):
        info['type'] = 'bool'
    elif len(item['raw']) > 1 or item['raw'][0].rstrip().endswith('\\'):
        info['type'] = 'list'
    else:
        info['type'] = 'string'
    return info

if __name__ == '__main__':
    header, items = parse(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])
    out = {'header': header, 'items': []}
    for it in items:
        if it['kind'] == 'section':
            out['items'].append(it)
        else:
            r = infer(it)
            r['kind'] = 'tag'
            r['raw'] = it['raw']
            out['items'].append(r)
    json.dump(out, open(sys.argv[3], 'w'), indent=1)
    ntag = sum(1 for x in out['items'] if x['kind']=='tag')
    print(f'sections={sum(1 for x in out["items"] if x["kind"]=="section")} tags={ntag}')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Probe the reference binary through its normal CLI (-x) to classify each
config tag as bool / int / enum / list / string, and to discover the accepted
enum spellings.  Purely black-box: we feed values in and read warnings out."""
import json, re, subprocess, sys, os, tempfile

BIN = '/workspace/executable'

def run_x(text, cwd):
    p = os.path.join(cwd, 'P')
    open(p, 'w').write(text)
    r = subprocess.run([BIN, '-x', 'P'], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout + r.stderr

def main():
    d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
    cwd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    tags = [x for x in d['items'] if x['kind'] == 'tag']
    for t in tags:
        n = t['name']
        out = run_x(f'{n} = a b\n', cwd)
        if 'not a valid boolean value' in out:
            t['type'] = 'bool'
        elif 'not a valid number in the range' in out:
            m = re.search(r'range \[(-?\d+)\.\.(-?\d+)\]', out)
            t['type'] = 'int'; t['min'] = int(m.group(1)); t['max'] = int(m.group(2))
        elif 'not a valid enum value' in out:
            t['type'] = 'enum'
        elif re.search(r'^%s\s+= a \\$' % n, out, re.M):
            t['type'] = 'list'
        else:
            t['type'] = 'string'
    # discover enum spellings from candidate words in the doc text
    for t in tags:
        if t['type'] != 'enum': continue
        doc = '\n'.join(t['doc'])
        cands = set(re.findall(r'\b([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:[-:][A-Za-z0-9_]+)*)\b', doc))
        cands |= set(t.get('values') or [])
        cands |= set(t['default'])
        good = []
        for c in sorted(cands):
            out = run_x(f'{t["name"]} = {c}\n', cwd)
            if 'not a valid enum value' not in out:
                good.append(c)
        t['values'] = good
    json.dump(d, open(sys.argv[2], 'w'), indent=1)
    import collections
    print(collections.Counter(x['type'] for x in tags))

main()
